benchmark: bits per character on held-out Bulgarian
why_this_metric: Per-token cross-entropy is not comparable across tokenizers. Nats over the same characters is: bpc = nats / (chars * ln 2).

protocol.text: thebogko/bulgarian-grammar-mistakes + thebogko/bulgarian-spelling-mistakes, the `correct` column, deduplicated, grammar set first
protocol.window: 256 tokens, non-overlapping; the first token of each window is never predicted
protocol.chars_covered: 49,217 (ours) / 49,590 (Gemma-2) / 49,528 (Gemma-3) — whole 256-token windows, so coverage differs slightly by tokenizer

reading: A loss, and it is on the card: 0.144 bpc behind the better of two much larger, continued-pretrained models. Worth noting which one is better — Gemma-2-2.6B beats Gemma-3-4B here despite being older and smaller.
measured_on: CUDA (Modal A10G), 2026-08-01, fp32 for ours and bf16 for the BgGPT arms
device_note: Forward passes over frozen weights, so this is reference numerics rather than a training measurement. Training comparisons in this project are CUDA-only for exactly the reason this is not: MPS and CUDA can disagree well beyond seed noise while a model is learning.
reproduced: CPU, 2026-07-28, under the superseded 12,000-char protocol: 1.3118 for ckpt_gpt2bg with chars_covered 11,690. The current numbers are the ~50,000-char CUDA run.
tolerance: the fourth decimal moves with float reassociation across devices; a rerun differing by more than 0.001 bpc means the text or the window changed, not the hardware

superseded.why: a 11.7k-character slice, chosen when the 2.6B baseline ran on a laptop; the cloud path made ~50k affordable and it is the better sample.
